newsitem.title: USA: 'Volcano' rumbles to top of weekend box office.
newsitem.headline: 'Volcano' rumbles to top of weekend box office.

text.p: "Volcano" erupted at the box office over the weekend, reaching in the top position with $14.7 million in ticket sales, according to studio estimates released Sunday.
Another newcomer, "Romy and Michelle's High School Reunion," was a distant second with $7.6 million. "Anaconda," the box office champ for the past two weekends, followed in third with $7.3 million.
"Volcano," a special-effects extravaganza starring Tommy Lee Jones and Anne Heche, depicts a geologically unlikely eruption in Los Angeles.
Released by 20th Century Fox and reportedly costing about $100 million to make, it averaged a reasonable $5,301 from each of 2,773 screens.
Its gross compared with the $18.5 million opening for the similarly themed "Dante's Peak" in February.

The two movies were set to be released within weeks of each other before Fox decided to delay "Volcano" until now. "Dante's Peak," released by Seagram Co. Ltd's Universal Pictures, has earned about $65 million.
According to a Variety poll of reviews in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington, 10 critics liked "Volcano," nine did not and 16 were mixed.
Considerably more popular with critics was "Romy and Michelle's High School Reunion," a comedy starring Mira Sorvina and Lisa Kudrow as two ditzy blondes who make waves at their 10-year reunion.
Variety said 16 critics liked it, one did not (USA Today) and eight were mixed. Released by Walt Disney Co., it averaged $4,744 from 1,602 screens.
"Anaconda's" 17-day total rose to $43.2 million. This weekend, the snake thriller averaged $2,972 from 2,456 screens. It is released by Sony Corp.'s Columbia Pictures.
Jim Carrey's "Liar Liar" slipped two places to fourth with $6.8 million in its sixth weekend. The Universal comedy has now earned $143.5 million, making it the highest grossing film released in 1997.

"The Saint" showed strong staying power as it fell one place to fifth in its fourth weekend. Its $5 million take propelled the cumulative gross to $48.2 million. Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc., released the Val Kilmer thriller.
